plan.plan:
CAPACITY PLAN IMPLEMENTATION - MESSAGE QUEUE AT 4,200 MSG/S PEAK WITH 3X BURST ALLOWANCE

Deliverable: one capacity-plan document containing an assumptions register plus three required sections (Sizing, Cost, Operations). Every figure below is the exact value the document must contain; all figures are formula-derived from a single workload model so any input change propagates deterministically, and Step 5 cross-checks every shared figure across the three sections.

STEP 0 - ASSUMPTIONS REGISTER (section 1 of the document)
The request leaves several parameters open; the plan fixes them as explicit assumptions, each flagged for stakeholder confirmation in Step 6:
- Technology: Apache Kafka 3.7+ in KRaft mode, self-hosted on AWS EC2 in us-east-1. Chosen over RabbitMQ because a durable 3x burst (12,600 msg/s) with replay and horizontal broker scaling is a log-shaped workload; RabbitMQ quorum queues would require tighter per-node tuning at this burst rate.
- Message definition: one Kafka record = one logical event; average 5.0 KB serialized including key and headers; distribution 60% at 1 KB, 30% at 8 KB, 10% at 20 KB (weighted average 0.6x1 + 0.3x8 + 0.1x20 = 5.0 KB); max record size 1 MB.
- Burst definition: 3x peak = 12,600 msg/s, sustained up to 15 minutes (900 s), at most 4 burst events per rolling 24 h, separated by at least 30 min, with the resulting consumer backlog fully drained within 30 min of burst end.
- Durability: replication factor (RF) 3, min.insync.replicas 2, producer acks=all, unclean leader election disabled, EBS encrypted at rest, TLS 1.2+ in transit.
- Availability target: 99.9% monthly for the produce path.
- Latency target: p99 produce-to-consume <= 500 ms at peak sustained (4,200 msg/s). During burst, per-message delay is bounded by the 30-min drain objective, not by 500 ms; if sub-second latency during burst is required, consumers must instead scale to 12,600 msg/s (flagged in Step 6).
- Retention: 24 hours, time-based, no compaction.
- Topology: 2 consumer groups, each reading the full stream (fan-out x2); producers and consumers deployed across the same 3 AZs as brokers with AZ-affine client routing so producer-to-broker traffic stays intra-AZ.
- Average steady ingress for cost averaging only: 50% of peak sustained = 2,100 msg/s = 10.5 MB/s.
- Currency / region / horizon: USD, AWS us-east-1 public on-demand pricing, 12-month horizon; prices are planning figures as of the plan date and must be re-verified at purchase.
- Compression: not counted (payloads treated as incompressible); producer-side zstd is noted as a cost-reduction lever only.

STEP 1 - CANONICAL WORKLOAD MODEL (section 2; single source of truth for all numbers)
Decimal units (1 KB = 1,000 B):
- Peak sustained: 4,200 msg/s x 5.0 KB = 21.0 MB/s payload ingress.
- Burst: 12,600 msg/s (= 3 x 4,200) x 5.0 KB = 63.0 MB/s payload ingress.
- Cluster disk write at RF 3: 63.0 MB/s peak sustained; 189.0 MB/s burst.
- Volume per copy per day, worst case (peak sustained held for the full 24 h retention plus bursts): 21.0 MB/s x 86,400 s = 1,814.4 GB, plus 4 bursts x 900 s x 63.0 MB/s = 226.8 GB, total 2,041.2 GB per copy per day.
- Burst backlog per event: (12,600 - 4,200) msg/s x 900 s = 7,560,000 messages = 37.8 GB.
- Consumer drain requirement: each group must sustain 8,400 msg/s (2 x peak sustained = 42.0 MB/s) so net drain = 8,400 - 4,200 = 4,200 msg/s and 7,560,000 / 4,200 = 1,800 s = 30 min, meeting the recovery objective exactly at worst case.

STEP 2 - SIZING SECTION (section 3 of the document; content as follows)
2.1 Broker count = 6 (2 per AZ across 3 AZs) plus 3 dedicated KRaft controller nodes (1 per AZ). Derivation from four constraints:
- Disk throughput: burst cluster write 189.0 MB/s with one broker down must stay <= 40% of the per-broker provisioned 250 MB/s: 189 / (N-1) <= 100, so N >= 3 (not binding).
- CPU: per-broker produce rate at burst with one broker down must stay <= ~3,000 msg/s per 8-vCPU broker (keeps CPU <= ~40%): 12,600 / (N-1) <= 3,000, so N >= 6 (binding).
- Storage: per-broker worst-case usage 2,041.2 GB x 3 / N must stay <= 75% of a 1,500 GB volume (1,125 GB): N >= 5.44 (binding).
- AZ spread: N must be a multiple of 3 for even placement. Result: N = 6.
2.2 Instance: EC2 m6i.2xlarge per broker (8 vCPU, 32 GiB, >= 10 Gbps network). JVM heap 8 GiB; remaining ~24 GiB as page cache, covering roughly 19 min of peak-sustained tail writes (24 GB / 21.0 MB/s) for warm consumer fetches; older reads are served from EBS within provisioned throughput.
2.3 Storage per broker: single EBS gp3 volume, 1,500 GB, provisioned at 250 MB/s and 6,000 IOPS.
- Worst-case usage: 2,041.2 x 3 / 6 = 1,020.6 GB = 68% of 1,500 GB; typical (average-rate) usage 567 GB = 37.8%.
- Worst-case disk throughput: burst with one broker down = 189 / 5 = 37.8 MB/s writes plus up to ~31.6 MB/s cold consumer reads = ~70 MB/s = 28% of 250 MB/s.
- Sensitivity: each additional day of retention adds 1,020.6 GB (~USD 81.65/month per broker at USD 0.08/GB-month).
2.4 Partitions: 48 on the main topic, RF 3, leader-balanced (8 leaders + 16 followers per broker). Per-partition burst rate = 12,600 / 48 = ~262 msg/s. 48 partitions allow up to 48 consumers per group; draining at 8,400 msg/s needs ~175 msg/s per consumer.
2.5 Network: worst case per broker (burst, one broker down, +25% protocol/TLS overhead): produce 63/5 x 1.25 = 15.75 MB/s, replication 126/5 x 1.25 = 31.5 MB/s, consumer egress 126/5 x 1.25 = 31.5 MB/s; total ~79 MB/s = ~0.63 Gbps = ~6.3% of the 10 Gbps link.
2.6 Failure tolerance:
- One broker down: all targets hold (numbers in 2.3 and 2.5).
- One AZ down (4 brokers remain): per-broker burst write 189/4 = 47.25 MB/s (18.9% of 250 MB/s); per-broker rate 12,600/4 = 3,150 msg/s, slightly above the 3,000 guide but within engineering margin; the produce path stays available because each partition keeps ISR >= 2 (RF 3, one replica per AZ).
- Rolling maintenance: one broker at a time; min.insync.replicas 2 keeps acks=all writes available throughout.
2.7 Growth: scale-out trigger = rolling 30-day peak sustained exceeds 6,300 msg/s (1.5x design point) or burst budget breached twice in a month. Action: expand 6 -> 9 brokers (3 per AZ), re-partition 48 -> 72, rebalance with Cruise Control; per-broker worst-case storage drops to 2,041.2 x 3 / 9 = 680.4 GB.

STEP 3 - COST SECTION (section 4; priced per broker, USD, us-east-1, on-demand, 730 h/month)
3.1 Per-broker monthly line items:
- EC2 m6i.2xlarge: 0.384 USD/h x 730 h = 280.32
- EBS gp3 data volume 1,500 GB x 0.08 USD/GB-month = 120.00
- gp3 provisioned throughput 250 MB/s (125 above free baseline) x 0.04 = 5.00
- gp3 provisioned IOPS 6,000 (3,000 above baseline) x 0.005 = 15.00
- Cross-AZ data transfer = 189.00, composed of: steady state at 10.5 MB/s average payload - replication to 2 out-of-AZ followers = 21.0 MB/s cluster-wide, consumer fetches 2 groups x 10.5 = 21.0 MB/s x 2/3 crossing AZ = 14.0 MB/s, total 35.0 MB/s / 6 brokers = 5.83 MB/s per broker x 2,592,000 s (30 days) = 15,120 GB; burst - 4 x 900 s = 3,600 s/day at burst rates, replication 126 MB/s + fetch cross-AZ 84 MB/s = 210 MB/s cluster / 6 = 35 MB/s per broker x 3,600 s = 126 GB/day x 30 = 3,780 GB/month; total (15,120 + 3,780) = 18,900 GB x 0.01 USD/GB = 189.00.
- PER-BROKER TOTAL: 609.32 USD/month.
3.2 Cluster rollup: 6 brokers x 609.32 = 3,655.92; control plane 3 x m6i.large KRaft controllers (0.096 USD/h x 730 = 70.08 each, plus 100 GB gp3 at 8.00 = 78.08 each) = 234.24; TOTAL 3,890.16 USD/month = 46,681.92 USD/year.
3.3 Options and sensitivities (clearly labeled, not part of headline totals):
- 1-yr Compute Savings Plan (~30% off EC2): per broker ~525.22/month; cluster ~3,322.50/month.
- If AZ-affine client routing is not implemented, producer cross-AZ adds ~37.80 USD/month per broker.
- Each extra day of retention: +81.65 USD/month per broker.
- Byte-derived figures scale linearly with message size: at 10 KB average, per-broker cost becomes 280.32 + 240.00 + 5.00 + 15.00 + 378.00 = 918.32 USD/month.
- Monitoring (Prometheus, Grafana, Alertmanager, JMX/node/kafka exporters) assumed on existing shared infrastructure at 0 incremental cost; otherwise add 1 x m6i.large at 70.08 USD/month. The exporters themselves run on the existing broker and controller instances.

STEP 4 - OPERATIONS SECTION (section 5; alert thresholds and procedures)
4.1 Burst budget policy (restates sizing figures): a burst event is cluster produce rate > 4,200 msg/s for >= 60 s. Budget: <= 4 events per rolling 24 h, each <= 15 min, spaced >= 30 min, backlog drained <= 30 min after event end. Consumers provisioned for 8,400 msg/s per group.
4.2 Alert thresholds (each row cites its sizing derivation):
- Cluster produce rate: Warning > 12,600 msg/s sustained 5 min; Critical > 12,600 msg/s sustained 15 min. Derivation: burst ceiling = 3 x 4,200; 15 min = max burst duration.
- Burst frequency: Warning > 4 burst events in rolling 24 h. Derivation: burst budget.
- Burst overlap: Critical if a burst event starts while consumer lag from a prior burst is > 0. Derivation: 30-min spacing/drain rule.
- Consumer lag per group: Warning > 252,000 messages (60 s x 4,200 msg/s) sustained 5 min; Critical > 756,000 (180 s x 4,200) sustained 5 min. Derivation: latency target at peak sustained.
- Drain breach: Critical if lag > 0 persists 30 min after burst-event end. Derivation: recovery objective.
- Broker CPU: Warning >= 50% sustained 10 min; Critical >= 70% sustained 5 min. Derivation: engineered worst case ~40% (burst, one broker down).
- Disk throughput: Warning >= 50% of 250 MB/s (125 MB/s) sustained 15 min; Critical >= 75% (187.5 MB/s) sustained 5 min. Derivation: worst case ~70 MB/s (28%).
- Disk IOPS: Warning >= 80% of 6,000 (4,800) sustained 10 min; Critical >= 95% (5,700) sustained 5 min. Transient warnings inside declared burst windows are expected; persistent warnings outside bursts trigger re-provisioning to 9,000 IOPS (+15.00 USD/month per broker).
- Disk space: Warning >= 75% of 1,500 GB (1,125 GB); Critical >= 85% (1,275 GB); Critical if projected time-to-full < 6 h. Derivation: worst-case steady usage 1,020.6 GB (68%).
- Network per broker: Warning >= 40% of 10 Gbps sustained 10 min; Critical >= 70% sustained 5 min. Derivation: worst case ~0.63 Gbps (6.3%).
- Under-replicated partitions: Warning >= 1 for 10 min; Critical >= 12 (25% of 48) for 5 min; Offline partitions >= 1: Critical immediately.
- UnderMinIsr partitions >= 1: Critical immediately (acks=all writes failing).
- Active controller count != 1: Critical immediately (KRaft quorum health).
- Broker down (process/TCP 9093): Critical after 1 min; page immediately if it occurs during an active burst event.
- Request handler idle ratio: Warning < 0.30 sustained 5 min; Critical < 0.10.
- Network processor idle ratio: Warning < 0.30 sustained 5 min; Critical < 0.10.
- Produce/consume error rate (timeouts, NotEnoughReplicas): Warning > 0.1% of requests sustained 5 min; Critical > 1%.
- Swap usage: Warning > 0; Critical > 512 MB.
- TLS certificate expiry: Warning < 21 days; Critical < 7 days.
4.3 Runbooks (one paragraph each in the document): burst response (verify budget, watch drain, scale consumers to 8,400 msg/s per group); broker replacement (one at a time, min.insync 2 keeps writes up, re-replicate via Cruise Control); disk pressure (raise retention cleanup, re-provision IOPS/throughput, scale out per 2.7); scale-out 6 -> 9 per 2.7; rolling upgrade (one broker at a time, controllers one at a time).
4.4 Pre-production validation test (must pass before go-live): sustain 4,200 msg/s for 1 h, then 12,600 msg/s for 15 min with one broker cordoned; acceptance: produce error rate < 0.1%, no UnderMinIsr, per-broker CPU < 50%, per-broker disk throughput < 125 MB/s, backlog drained within 30 min of burst end.

STEP 5 - CROSS-SECTION CONSISTENCY CHECK (perform before delivery)
Verify each shared figure appears identically in every section that cites it:
- 4,200 msg/s and 12,600 msg/s (3x): Sizing 2.1/2.4/2.6, Cost 3.1 (burst network math), Operations 4.1/4.2 (produce-rate, burst-frequency, lag thresholds).
- 21.0 MB/s and 63.0 MB/s payload: Model Step 1, Sizing 2.2/2.5, Cost 3.1, Operations derivations.
- 189.0 MB/s cluster burst write and 37.8 MB/s per broker with one broker down: Sizing 2.1/2.3, Operations 4.2 disk-throughput derivation.
- 15 min / 4 per day / 30 min drain / 8,400 msg/s consumer capacity: Model Step 1, Sizing 2.4, Cost 3.1 (burst seconds per month), Operations 4.1/4.2.
- 6 brokers, 48 partitions, RF 3, min.insync 2: Sizing 2.1/2.4/2.6, Cost 3.2 (multiplier), Operations 4.2 (URP thresholds).
- 1,500 GB / 250 MB/s / 6,000 IOPS per broker and 1,020.6 GB worst-case usage: Sizing 2.3, Cost 3.1 (120.00 / 5.00 / 15.00), Operations 4.2 (disk thresholds).
- 609.32 per broker, 3,890.16 per month, 46,681.92 per year: Cost 3.1/3.2; Operations 4.2 cites the +15.00 IOPS re-provision delta consistently.
- 5.0 KB average, 24 h retention, 2 consumer groups, 10.5 MB/s average ingress: Assumptions Step 0, Model Step 1, Cost 3.1.

STEP 6 - STAKEHOLDER CONFIRMATION AND CHANGE CONTROL
- Circulate the assumptions register (Step 0) for confirmation; any change to message size, retention, rates, burst definition, consumer count, or region triggers recomputation via the formulas in Steps 1-3.
- Confirm whether sub-second latency during burst is required; if yes, consumer provisioning changes from 8,400 to 12,600 msg/s per group and the 30-min drain objective is retired.
- Re-verify AWS pricing at purchase; the document carries a stated pricing date.
success_criteria: The delivered plan states 4,200 msg/s peak sustained and 12,600 msg/s (3x) burst in the sizing, cost, and operations sections, with the derived byte rates 21.0 MB/s and 63.0 MB/s (at the stated 5.0 KB average message size) appearing identically everywhere they are cited.

The sizing section specifies exactly 6 brokers (EC2 m6i.2xlarge, 2 per AZ across 3 AZs, RF 3, min.insync.replicas 2, 48 partitions) plus 3 KRaft controllers, and shows the degraded-mode burst calculation 189.0 MB/s across 5 remaining brokers = 37.8 MB/s per broker against the provisioned 250 MB/s gp3 volume of 1,500 GB at 6,000 IOPS.

The cost section itemizes each broker at USD 609.32/month (EC2 280.32 + EBS 120.00 + throughput 5.00 + IOPS 15.00 + cross-AZ 189.00) and rolls up to USD 3,890.16/month and USD 46,681.92/year including the 3 controller nodes at USD 78.08 each.

The operations section encodes the burst budget as alerts tied to the same numbers: produce rate above 12,600 msg/s for 5 minutes warns and for 15 minutes pages; more than 4 burst events in a rolling 24 h warns; a burst starting before the prior backlog drains, or backlog persisting 30 minutes after burst end, pages.

Every alert threshold in the operations section cites a sizing derivation that matches the sizing figures: disk-space warning at 75% of 1,500 GB (1,125 GB) and critical at 85% (1,275 GB) sit above the modeled worst-case usage of 1,020.6 GB per broker, and the CPU warning of 50% sits above the engineered burst worst case of about 40%.

The plan contains an assumptions register (5.0 KB average with the 60/30/10 size distribution, 24 h retention, 2 consumer groups, average ingress at 50% of peak, USD us-east-1 on-demand pricing, 12-month horizon) and a scale-out rule expanding from 6 to 9 brokers when the rolling 30-day peak sustained rate exceeds 6,300 msg/s.

- Type: capacity plan (Assumptions Register + Sizing + Cost + Operations)
- Currency / region / horizon: USD, AWS us-east-1 public on-demand, 12-month horizon
- Pricing date: plan date (planning figures; must be re-verified at purchase)

- Citation keys: subsection labels 2.x (Sizing), 3.x (Cost), 4.x (Operations) are retained as the plan's canonical keys and are the keys used by the cross-check in Section 6. "Model" = Section 2.

---

## SECTION 1 — ASSUMPTIONS REGISTER (Step 0)

During burst, per-message delay is bounded by the 30-min drain objective, not by 500 ms; if sub-second latency during burst is required, consumers must instead scale to 12,600 msg/s (flagged in Section 7). | YES |
| A-07 | Retention | 24 hours, time-based, no compaction. | YES |
| A-08 | Topology | 2 consumer groups, each reading the full stream (fan-out ×2); producers and consumers deployed across the same 3 AZs as brokers with AZ-affine client routing so producer-to-broker traffic stays intra-AZ. | YES |

| A-10 | Currency / region / horizon | USD, AWS us-east-1 public on-demand pricing, 12-month horizon; prices are planning figures as of the plan date and must be re-verified at purchase. | YES |
| A-11 | Compression | Not counted (payloads treated as incompressible); producer-side zstd is noted as a cost-reduction lever only. | YES |

---

## SECTION 2 — CANONICAL WORKLOAD MODEL (Step 1; single source of truth)

Decimal units: 1 KB = 1,000 B. Every figure in Sections 3, 4 and 5 traces to this table.

| # | Quantity | Formula | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| M1 | Peak sustained payload ingress | 4,200 msg/s × 5.0 KB | 21.0 MB/s |
| M2 | Burst payload ingress | 12,600 msg/s (= 3 × 4,200) × 5.0 KB | 63.0 MB/s |
| M3 | Cluster disk write at RF 3, peak sustained | 21.0 MB/s × 3 | 63.0 MB/s |
| M4 | Cluster disk write at RF 3, burst | 63.0 MB/s × 3 | 189.0 MB/s |
| M5 | Volume per copy per day, worst case (peak sustained held full 24 h retention + bursts) | 21.0 MB/s × 86,400 s = 1,814.4 GB; plus 4 bursts × 900 s × 63.0 MB/s = 226.8 GB | 2,041.2 GB per copy per day |
| M6 | Burst backlog per event | (12,600 − 4,200) msg/s × 900 s | 7,560,000 messages = 37.8 GB |
| M7 | Consumer drain requirement per group | 2 × peak sustained = 8,400 msg/s = 42.0 MB/s; net drain 8,400 − 4,200 = 4,200 msg/s; 7,560,000 / 4,200 | 1,800 s = 30 min, meeting the recovery objective exactly at worst case |
| M8 | Average steady ingress (A-09) | 50% × 4,200 = 2,100 msg/s × 5.0 KB | 10.5 MB/s |

---

## SECTION 3 — SIZING

### 2.1 Broker count = 6 (2 per AZ across 3 AZs) plus 3 dedicated KRaft controller nodes (1 per AZ)

Derivation from four constraints (N = data brokers):

| Constraint | Requirement | Solve | Binding? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Disk throughput | Burst cluster write 189.0 MB/s with one broker down must stay ≤ 40% of the per-broker provisioned 250 MB/s | 189 / (N−1) ≤ 100 → N ≥ 3 | No |
| CPU | Per-broker produce rate at burst with one broker down must stay ≤ ~3,000 msg/s per 8-vCPU broker (keeps CPU ≤ ~40%) | 12,600 / (N−1) ≤ 3,000 → N ≥ 6 | Yes (binding) |
| Storage | Per-broker worst-case usage 2,041.2 GB × 3 / N must stay ≤ 75% of a 1,500 GB volume (1,125 GB) | N ≥ 6,123.6 / 1,125 → N ≥ 5.44 | Yes (binding) |
| AZ spread | N must be a multiple of 3 for even placement | N ∈ {3, 6, 9, …} | Shaping |

Result: N = 6. Topology: brokers b1–b6 (2 per AZ × 3 AZs), controllers c1–c3 (1 per AZ), replication factor 3, min.insync.replicas 2.

### 2.2 Instance: EC2 m6i.2xlarge per broker (8 vCPU, 32 GiB, ≥ 10 Gbps network)

JVM heap 8 GiB; remaining ~24 GiB as page cache, covering roughly 19 min of peak-sustained tail writes (24 GB / 21.0 MB/s ≈ 1,143 s) for warm consumer fetches; older reads are served from EBS within provisioned throughput.

### 2.3 Storage per broker: single EBS gp3 volume, 1,500 GB, provisioned at 250 MB/s and 6,000 IOPS

- Worst-case usage: 2,041.2 × 3 / 6 = 1,020.6 GB = 68% of 1,500 GB.
- Typical (average-rate) usage: (10.5 MB/s × 86,400 s = 907.2 GB) + 226.8 GB bursts = 1,134.0 GB per copy per day × 3 / 6 = 567.0 GB = 37.8%.
- Worst-case disk throughput: burst with one broker down = 189 / 5 = 37.8 MB/s writes plus up to ~31.6 MB/s cold consumer reads = ~70 MB/s = 28% of 250 MB/s.
- Sensitivity: each additional day of retention adds 1,020.6 GB (~USD 81.65/month per broker at USD 0.08/GB-month).

### 2.4 Partitions: 48 on the main topic, RF 3, leader-balanced (8 leaders + 16 followers per broker)

- Per-partition burst rate = 12,600 / 48 ≈ 262 msg/s.
- 48 partitions allow up to 48 consumers per group; draining at 8,400 msg/s needs ~175 msg/s per consumer (8,400 / 48).

### 2.5 Network (worst case per broker: burst, one broker down, +25% protocol/TLS overhead)

| Component | Formula | Rate |
|---|---|---|
| Produce | 63 / 5 × 1.25 | 15.75 MB/s |
| Replication | 126 / 5 × 1.25 | 31.5 MB/s |
| Consumer egress | 126 / 5 × 1.25 | 31.5 MB/s |
| Total | 15.75 + 31.5 + 31.5 | ~79 MB/s ≈ 0.63 Gbps ≈ 6.3% of 10 Gbps |

(Replication traffic = 2 of 3 replicas = 189 / 3 × 2 = 126 MB/s cluster-wide at burst; consumer egress = 63 MB/s × 2 groups = 126 MB/s cluster-wide at burst.)

### 2.6 Failure tolerance

- One broker down: all targets hold (numbers in 2.3 and 2.5: 37.8 MB/s write vs 250 MB/s; ~79 MB/s total network vs 10 Gbps).
- One AZ down (4 brokers remain): per-broker burst write 189 / 4 = 47.25 MB/s (18.9% of 250 MB/s); per-broker rate 12,600 / 4 = 3,150 msg/s, slightly above the 3,000 msg/s guide but within engineering margin; the produce path stays available because each partition keeps ISR ≥ 2 (RF 3, one replica per AZ).
- Rolling maintenance: one broker at a time; min.insync.replicas 2 keeps acks=all writes available throughout.

### 2.7 Growth

- Scale-out trigger: rolling 30-day peak sustained exceeds 6,300 msg/s (1.5× design point of 4,200) or burst budget (4.1) breached twice in a month.
- Action: expand 6 → 9 brokers (3 per AZ), re-partition 48 → 72, rebalance with Cruise Control; per-broker worst-case storage drops to 2,041.2 × 3 / 9 = 680.4 GB.

---

## SECTION 4 — COST

Priced per broker, USD, us-east-1, on-demand, 730 h/month. Byte-derived line items are derived from Section 2 (Model) at 5.0 KB average and 24 h retention.

### 3.1 Per-broker monthly line items

| Line item | Calculation | USD/month |
|---|---|---|
| EC2 m6i.2xlarge | 0.384 USD/h × 730 h | 280.32 |
| EBS gp3 data volume | 1,500 GB × 0.08 USD/GB-month | 120.00 |
| gp3 provisioned throughput | 250 MB/s (125 above free baseline) × 0.04 | 5.00 |
| gp3 provisioned IOPS | 6,000 (3,000 above baseline) × 0.005 | 15.00 |
| Cross-AZ data transfer | see decomposition below | 189.00 |
| PER-BROKER TOTAL | 280.32 + 120.00 + 5.00 + 15.00 + 189.00 | 609.32 |

### 3.2 Cluster rollup

| Component | Calculation | USD/month |
|---|---|---|
| 6 data brokers | 6 × 609.32 | 3,655.92 |

## SECTION 5 — OPERATIONS

### 4.1 Burst budget policy (restates sizing figures)

A burst event is cluster produce rate > 4,200 msg/s for ≥ 60 s. Budget: ≤ 4 events per rolling 24 h, each ≤ 15 min (900 s), spaced ≥ 30 min apart, backlog drained ≤ 30 min after event end. Consumers provisioned for 8,400 msg/s per group (M7). Burst ceiling 12,600 msg/s = 3 × 4,200 (M2).

### 4.2 Alert thresholds (each row cites its sizing derivation)

|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Cluster produce rate | > 12,600 msg/s sustained 5 min | > 12,600 msg/s sustained 15 min | Burst ceiling = 3 × 4,200 (M2, A-03); 15 min = max burst duration (A-03, 4.1) |
| 2 | Burst frequency | > 4 burst events in rolling 24 h | — | Burst budget (A-03, 4.1) |
| 3 | Burst overlap | — | A burst event starts while consumer lag from a prior burst is > 0 | 30-min spacing/drain rule (A-03, M6/M7) |
| 4 | Consumer lag per group | > 252,000 messages (60 s × 4,200 msg/s) sustained 5 min | > 756,000 messages (180 s × 4,200) sustained 5 min | Latency target at peak sustained (A-06, 2.4) |

### 4.3 Runbooks

Burst response: confirm the event is within budget (≤ 4 events per rolling 24 h, ≥ 30 min since the previous event, ≤ 15 min duration) before treating it as normal operation; watch per-group consumer lag against 252,000 / 756,000 message thresholds and the drain clock; scale consumers so each group sustains 8,400 msg/s (M7), which yields a net drain of 4,200 msg/s and clears the 7,560,000-message backlog in 1,800 s (30 min); if lag from a prior burst is still > 0 when a new burst starts, page immediately (alert 3).

Broker replacement: replace exactly one broker at a time; with RF 3 and min.insync.replicas 2, acks=all writes remain available throughout (2.6); after the replacement, re-replicate and re-balance leadership with Cruise Control, verifying under-replicated partitions return to 0 within 10 min (alert 11) and that per-broker worst-case storage returns to ≤ 1,020.6 GB (2.3).

Disk pressure: first confirm the driver (retention overrun vs. ingest spike); raise/force retention cleanup back to the 24-hour time-based policy (A-07), re-provision gp3 throughput/IOPS (6,000 → 9,000 IOPS at +15.00 USD/month per broker) if warnings persist outside declared burst windows, and if projected time-to-full is < 6 h or usage passes 1,275 GB (85%), execute the scale-out per 2.7 rather than extending retention.

Scale-out 6 → 9: trigger on rolling 30-day peak sustained > 6,300 msg/s or two burst-budget breaches in a month (2.7); add one broker per AZ (3 total), re-partition 48 → 72 with Cruise Control, and verify worst-case per-broker storage falls to 680.4 GB and per-broker burst CPU returns below the ~40% guide before decommissioning old capacity.

Rolling upgrade: upgrade data brokers one at a time (never two in the same AZ), waiting for under-replicated partitions to clear and ISR to return to 3 before the next node; then upgrade the 3 KRaft controllers one at a time, verifying active controller count = 1 (alert 13) after each step; min.insync.replicas 2 keeps acks=all writes available for the whole sequence (2.6).

### 4.4 Pre-production validation test (must pass before go-live)

Procedure: sustain 4,200 msg/s for 1 h, then 12,600 msg/s for 15 min with one broker cordoned. Acceptance: produce error rate < 0.1%, no UnderMinIsr, per-broker CPU < 50%, per-broker disk throughput < 125 MB/s, and backlog drained within 30 min of burst end.
